evidence.observation: processProxyEvent validates each incoming proxy event against the partial message built so far and throws a stable, descriptive Error (for example 'Received text_delta for non-text content') instead of mutating content it does not match. The guard on the target content type runs before any write, so an invalid event is rejected before it can change message state. This is the reject-before-effect pattern the demo adapter transfers to its validate step.

streamProxy is the single public boundary of the proxy stream. It wraps the whole request in one try/catch and funnels every failure path - a non-OK HTTP response normalized into 'Proxy error: <status|error>', a thrown validation error, an aborted signal, or a clean EOF without a terminal event - into the same normalized error event { type: 'error', reason, error } with partial.stopReason and partial.errorMessage set. Consumers therefore only ever see one stable error shape, which is the normalization the demo adapter mirrors in its single catch around handleCommand.

ProxyAssistantMessageEvent is the closed discriminated union of wire events. It fixes exactly one terminal error variant with reason (aborted | error), optional errorMessage, usage, and providerThinkingLevel, and is exhaustively switched on in processProxyEvent (default branch asserts never). This closed error shape is the contract the demo adapter copies as its single AdapterError with a fixed code set.

claims.claim: packages/agent/src/proxy.ts rejects invalid input before it can take effect: processProxyEvent type-checks each event against the target content slot and throws a stable message before mutating the partial message, and streamProxy's non-OK HTTP branch normalizes the failure before any stream data is read.

packages/agent/src/proxy.ts surfaces all failures through one stable error shape: every throw, abort, dropped stream, or bad HTTP status is caught by streamProxy and emitted as { type: 'error', reason, error } with stopReason and errorMessage populated, matching the single error variant of ProxyAssistantMessageEvent.

The demo adapter (.prale-eval/demo/rpc-command-adapter.ts) transfers both behaviors locally: validate() is pure and rejects bad_request/unsupported_command before applyCommand touches state.effects, and a single catch in handleCommand normalizes validation errors, runtime misses, and unexpected internal throws into the one AdapterError shape with a closed code set.

conclusion: The proxy stream in packages/agent/src/proxy.ts already encodes the requested contract: validate the incoming event against current state and reject before mutating (processProxyEvent), and normalize every failure path into one stable error event via a single boundary catch (streamProxy). The demo at .prale-eval/demo/rpc-command-adapter.ts transfers that experience to a tiny local command/RPC adapter: validate() is pure and rejects malformed or unknown commands before applyCommand runs the fake effect, and handleCommand's single catch maps every rejection to one { ok: false, error: { code, message, command } } shape with a closed code set. Executing the demo shows invalid inputs leave state.effects unchanged while all rejections share identical keys.

validation.notes: Ran under Node v24.14.0 with built-in TypeScript type stripping; no dependencies installed and no install step required. Output: 8/8 checks PASS ('ALL CHECKS PASSED'), exit code 0. Checks confirm invalid input is rejected before the fake effect (effects list stays at 1 for all rejection cases and the stored value is untouched) and that all four rejection paths plus a forced internal failure normalize to the same error shape. The demo imports nothing from the workspace packages, so the absent node_modules tree is not a limitation.
